L1: # `subprocess` — Subprocess management【0†¶】
L2: 
L3: Source code: 【1†Lib/subprocess.py†github.com】
L4: 
L5: * * *
L6: 
L7: The 【0†`subprocess`】 module allows you to spawn new processes, connect to their input/output/error pipes, and obtain their return codes. This module intends to replace several older modules and functions:
L8: 
L9:     os.system
L10:     os.spawn*
L11: 
L12: 
L13: Information about how the 【0†`subprocess`】 module can be used to replace these modules and functions can be found in the following sections.
L14: 
L15: See also
L16: 【2†PEP 324†peps.python.org】 – PEP proposing the subprocess module
L17: 
L18: 【3†Availability】: not Emscripten, not WASI.
L19: 
L20: This module does not work or is not available on WebAssembly platforms `wasm32-emscripten` and `wasm32-wasi`. See 【4†WebAssembly platforms】 for more information.
L21: ## Using the 【0†`subprocess`】 Module【5†¶】
L22: 
L23: The recommended approach to invoking subprocesses is to use the 【6†`run()`】 function for all use cases it can handle. For more advanced use cases, the underlying 【7†`Popen`】 interface can be used directly.
L24: subprocess.run(args, * (Keyword-only parameters separator (PEP 3102)), stdin=None, input=None, stdout=None, stderr=None, capture_output=False, shell=False, cwd=None, timeout=None, check=False, encoding=None, errors=None, text=None, env=None, universal_newlines=None, **other_popen_kwargs)【6†¶】
L25: 
L26: 
L27: Run the command described by args. Wait for command to complete, then return a 【8†`CompletedProcess`】 instance.
L28: The arguments shown above are merely the most common ones, described below in 【9†Frequently Used Arguments】 (hence the use of keyword-only notation in the abbreviated signature). The full function signature is largely the same as that of the 【7†`Popen`】 constructor - most of the arguments to this function are passed through to that interface. (timeout, input, check, and capture_output are not.)
L29: If capture_output is true, stdout and stderr will be captured. When used, the internal 【7†`Popen`】 object is automatically created with stdout and stderr both set to 【10†`PIPE`】. The stdout and stderr arguments may not be supplied at the same time as capture_output. If you wish to capture and combine both streams into one, set stdout to 【10†`PIPE`】 and stderr to 【11†`STDOUT`】, instead of using capture_output.
L30: A timeout may be specified in seconds, it is internally passed on to 【12†`Popen.communicate()`】. If the timeout expires, the child process will be killed and waited for. The 【13†`TimeoutExpired`】 exception will be re-raised after the child process has terminated. The initial process creation itself cannot be interrupted on many platform APIs so you are not guaranteed to see a timeout exception until at least after however long process creation takes.
L31: The input argument is passed to 【12†`Popen.communicate()`】 and thus to the subprocess’s stdin. If used it must be a byte sequence, or a string if encoding or errors is specified or text is true. When used, the internal 【7†`Popen`】 object is automatically created with stdin set to 【10†`PIPE`】, and the stdin argument may not be used as well.
L32: If check is true, and the process exits with a non-zero exit code, a 【14†`CalledProcessError`】 exception will be raised. Attributes of that exception hold the arguments, the exit code, and stdout and stderr if they were captured.
L33: If encoding or errors are specified, or text is true, file objects for stdin, stdout and stderr are opened in text mode using the specified encoding and errors or the 【15†`io.TextIOWrapper`】 default. The universal_newlines argument is equivalent to text and is provided for backwards compatibility. By default, file objects are opened in binary mode.
L34: If env is not `None`, it must be a mapping that defines the environment variables for the new process; these are used instead of the default behavior of inheriting the current process’ environment. It is passed directly to 【7†`Popen`】. This mapping can be str to str on any platform or bytes to bytes on POSIX platforms much like 【16†`os.environ`】 or 【17†`os.environb`】.
L35: Examples:
L36: 
L37:     >>> subprocess.run(["ls", "-l"])  # doesn't capture output
L38:     CompletedProcess(args=['ls', '-l'], returncode=0)
L39: 
L40:     >>> subprocess.run("exit 1", shell=True, check=True)
L41:     Traceback (most recent call last):
L42:       ...
L43:     subprocess.CalledProcessError: Command 'exit 1' returned non-zero exit status 1
L44: 
L45:     >>> subprocess.run(["ls", "-l", "/dev/null"], capture_output=True)
L46:     CompletedProcess(args=['ls', '-l', '/dev/null'], returncode=0,
L47:     stdout=b'crw-rw-rw- 1 root root 1, 3 Jan 23 16:23 /dev/null\n', stderr=b'')
L48: Added in version 3.5.
L49: 
L50: Changed in version 3.6: Added encoding and errors parameters
L51: 
L52: Changed in version 3.7: Added the text parameter, as a more understandable alias of universal_newlines. Added the capture_output parameter.
L53: 
L54: Changed in version 3.12: Changed Windows shell search order for `shell=True`. The current directory and `%PATH%` are replaced with `%COMSPEC%` and `%SystemRoot%\System32\cmd.exe`. As a result, dropping a malicious program named `cmd.exe` into a current directory no longer works.
L55: class subprocess.CompletedProcess【8†¶】
L56: 
L57: 
L58: The return value from 【6†`run()`】, representing a process that has finished.
L59: 
L60: args【18†¶】
L61: 
L62: 
L63: The arguments used to launch the process. This may be a list or a string.
L64: 
L65: returncode【19†¶】
L66: 
L67: 
L68: Exit status of the child process. Typically, an exit status of 0 indicates that it ran successfully.
L69: 
L70: A negative value `-N` indicates that the child was terminated by signal `N` (POSIX only).
L71: 
L72: stdout【20†¶】
L73: Captured stdout from the child process. A bytes sequence, or a string if 【6†`run()`】 was called with an encoding, errors, or text=True. `None` if stdout was not captured.
L74: 
L75: If you ran the process with `stderr=subprocess.STDOUT`, stdout and stderr will be combined in this attribute, and 【21†`stderr`】 will be `None`.
L76: 
L77: stderr【21†¶】
L78: 
L79: 
L80: Captured stderr from the child process. A bytes sequence, or a string if 【6†`run()`】 was called with an encoding, errors, or text=True. `None` if stderr was not captured.
L81: check_returncode()【22†¶】
L82: 
L83: 
L84: If 【19†`returncode`】 is non-zero, raise a 【14†`CalledProcessError`】.
L85: 
L86: Added in version 3.5.
L87: 
L88: subprocess.DEVNULL【23†¶】
L89: 
L90: 
L91: Special value that can be used as the stdin, stdout or stderr argument to 【7†`Popen`】 and indicates that the special file 【24†`os.devnull`】 will be used.
L92: 
L93: Added in version 3.3.
L94: 
L95: subprocess.PIPE【10†¶】
L96: Special value that can be used as the stdin, stdout or stderr argument to 【7†`Popen`】 and indicates that a pipe to the standard stream should be opened. Most useful with 【12†`Popen.communicate()`】.
